$comment: Reparative programmes that were actually enacted and executed, entered to test one claim: that the obstacle to reparation is principle rather than feasibility. The load-bearing field is machinery - whether the programme required an instrument that did not already exist. If enacted programmes consistently reused ordinary appropriation, claims and settlement machinery, then operational capacity is not the binding constraint and the residual is a decision. The claim is falsifiable and the file is built so it can fail. beneficiary is kept separate from class because two of the largest programmes on record paid the holders of title rather than the people held. Figures are approximate where marked and no locator has been resolved against a source in this environment. See METHODOLOGY.md, Precedent and feasibility.

precedents.name: Slave Compensation Act 1837
precedents.harm: Abolition of slavery in the British colonies, treated as a taking from owners
precedents.class: Approximately 46,000 awards to slaveholders and mortgagees
precedents.amount: £20 million, on the order of 40 per cent of annual Treasury expenditure at the time, raised by loan
precedents.delivery: A purpose-built Commission of Slave Compensation adjudicated claims; awards paid through the Treasury
precedents.machinery_note: An ordinary appropriation and a claims commission. The commission was new; the instruments were not.
precedents.notes: The enslaved received nothing and were placed under apprenticeship. The public debt raised to pay the owners was reported by HM Treasury as finally discharged in 2015.

precedents.name: District of Columbia Compensated Emancipation Act
precedents.harm: Emancipation in the District, treated as a taking from owners
precedents.class: Slaveholders in the District who petitioned; approximately 3,100 people were freed
precedents.amount: Approximately $1 million appropriated, up to $300 per person held; separately up to $100 per freed person who agreed to emigrate
precedents.delivery: A board of three commissioners adjudicated petitions; payment through the Treasury
precedents.machinery_note: An appropriation and a three-member commission. No novel instrument was required to identify a class, adjudicate claims and pay them.
precedents.notes: The only occasion on which the United States enacted compensation for slavery. It ran to title. The freed person's entry in the scheme was an offer of money to leave the country.

precedents.name: Luxembourg Agreement and the Federal Compensation Law (BEG)
precedents.harm: Persecution, expropriation, forced labour and murder under the Nazi state
precedents.class: Survivors and heirs; a state and a representative organisation as collective payees
precedents.amount: DM 3 billion to Israel and DM 450 million to the Claims Conference under the 1952 agreement; individual pensions and lump sums under the BEG, continuing for decades
precedents.delivery: Treaty transfer plus a domestic compensation administration processing individual claims
precedents.machinery_note: A treaty and a domestic claims statute. Both are standing forms of instrument; the administration built to run them was new and was built.
precedents.notes: Establishes that a programme can run for generations, across borders, to a class defined by persecution rather than by residence, and can include collective as well as individual payees.

precedents.name: Tuskegee study settlement
precedents.harm: Forty years of withheld treatment under a federal research protocol
precedents.class: Surviving participants and the estates of those who had died; medical benefits later extended to wives, widows and children
precedents.delivery: Settlement of civil litigation, later a standing federal programme of medical benefits
precedents.machinery_note: Ordinary civil settlement. The extension of benefits to spouses and children required no new form of instrument.
precedents.notes: Reached the harmed without any criminal accountability. The corpus records the same entry as unpunished, which is the point of keeping the axes apart.

precedents.name: Civil Liberties Act of 1988
precedents.harm: Exclusion and mass incarceration of Japanese Americans during the Second World War
precedents.class: Surviving persons of Japanese ancestry who were interned, excluded or relocated
precedents.amount: $20,000 per person; on the order of 82,000 payments and approximately $1.6 billion
precedents.delivery: An Office of Redress Administration in the Department of Justice identified eligible people from wartime government records and paid them, with a formal apology, largely without requiring an application
precedents.machinery_note: An appropriation, an administrative office, and the government's own records used to find the claimants. The identification problem that is said to make reparation impossible was solved by reading the files the state had made while doing the harm.
precedents.notes: The central existence proof. A class defined by a historical wrong, located from administrative records, paid at national scale, within a presidential term.

precedents.name: Rosewood Claims Bill
precedents.harm: Destruction of the Black town of Rosewood in 1923 and the state's failure to protect or prosecute
precedents.class: Surviving residents, descendants with proven property loss, and a scholarship class
precedents.amount: Approximately $2.1 million, including payments to surviving residents, a property-loss fund for descendants, and a state scholarship fund
precedents.delivery: State claim bill, administered by the state
precedents.machinery_note: A legislative claim bill, the ordinary Florida instrument for paying a claim the courts cannot reach.
precedents.notes: A legislature paid a claim that was time-barred in every court. The statute of limitations is an impediment to a forum, not to a remedy.

precedents.name: North Carolina eugenics sterilisation compensation
precedents.harm: Compulsory sterilisation under the state eugenics programme
precedents.class: Living verified victims of the state programme
precedents.amount: $10 million fund, divided among roughly 220 verified claimants
precedents.delivery: A state office verified claims against the programme's own records; payments from 2014
precedents.machinery_note: An appropriation and a verification office working from the programme's surviving files.
precedents.notes: The verification burden fell on the claimant, and the fund was fixed rather than per capita, so the per-person sum depended on how many others were verified.

precedents.name: Chicago reparations ordinance for Burge-era police torture
precedents.harm: Torture of criminal suspects in police custody
precedents.class: Surviving victims with credible claims of torture by the commander and officers under him
precedents.amount: $5.5 million fund, up to $100,000 per survivor, for on the order of 57 people
precedents.delivery: City ordinance, with a counselling centre, free enrolment in the City Colleges for survivors and their families, a formal apology, and a required public-school curriculum on the torture
precedents.machinery_note: An ordinary municipal ordinance and appropriation.
precedents.notes: The only programme on file whose remedy includes a mandated curriculum. It treats the transmission of the record as part of what is owed, rather than as commemoration.

precedents.name: Evanston Local Reparations Restorative Housing Program
precedents.harm: Municipal housing discrimination against Black residents
precedents.class: Black residents of a defined qualifying period, and their direct descendants
precedents.amount: $10 million committed over ten years, funded from a local cannabis tax; initial housing benefit of $25,000 per qualifying recipient
precedents.delivery: Municipal programme with an eligibility period and a housing-directed benefit, later broadened to cash
precedents.machinery_note: A dedicated tax stream and a municipal benefit programme.
precedents.notes: The first municipal reparations programme in the United States addressed to housing discrimination, and the first to hypothecate a tax to it. Restricting the benefit to housing was contested by recipients.

precedents.name: Return of Bruce's Beach
precedents.harm: Condemnation and taking of a Black-owned beach resort in 1924
precedents.class: The identified descendants of the owners
precedents.amount: Return of the parcel itself; subsequently purchased from the family for a reported sum on the order of $20 million
precedents.delivery: State enabling legislation authorising the transfer, then a county conveyance to the descendants
precedents.machinery_note: Enabling legislation and an ordinary conveyance.
precedents.enacted_to_first_payment: About a year from enabling statute to transfer
precedents.notes: The only entry that delivers restitution in kind rather than compensation. It was reachable because the parcel was identifiable and the line of descent was provable - which is what the destruction of deeds elsewhere in the corpus was for.

precedents.name: Georgetown descendants fund
precedents.harm: The 1838 sale of 272 enslaved people by the Maryland Province of the Society of Jesus to fund the institution
precedents.amount: A student-approved fee, then an institutional commitment on the order of $400,000 a year, alongside a separate and much larger commitment announced by the Jesuit order
precedents.delivery: Institutional fund and admissions preference; genealogical identification of descendants from the sale records
precedents.machinery_note: An institution's own budget. Descendants were identified from the bill of sale - the commercial record produced to make title provable, proving the class now.
precedents.notes: Not a state programme, and entered as institutional so it cannot be counted as a governmental precedent. It is nonetheless the clearest demonstration that descendants of a documented 1838 sale can be identified individually.

precedents.name: Tulsa Race Riot Commission recommendations, not enacted
precedents.harm: Destruction of the Greenwood district in 1921
precedents.amount: Direct payments to survivors were recommended and not appropriated; a scholarship fund and a memorial followed
precedents.machinery_note: The programme was never enacted, so no machinery was tested. The commission established the facts; the legislature declined the remedy; the federal suit was dismissed as time-barred.
precedents.notes: The control case, and the reason this file exists. A state commission found the facts and recommended payment; what failed was not identification, not valuation, and not administration. It is entered so that the feasibility claim can be tested against a refusal rather than only against successes.
